title: Consumers Report Diverging Credit Market Experiences and Expectations

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York released its June 2017 SCE Credit Access Survey showing a spike in credit application rates to a series high (50.6%) alongside increased rejection rates (10.7% of applicants rejected), indicating diverging credit market experiences. Discouraged borrowers—those who didn't apply despite needing credit—fell to a series low of 5.9%, while both voluntary and involuntary credit account closures reached multi-year highs.
key_points: Credit application rates rose sharply to 50.6% in June 2017 from 46.1% in February 2017, a series high since October 2013
Rejection rates increased to 10.7% from 8.0% in February, with per-applicant rejection rate rising to 21.2% from 17.4%
Discouraged borrowers (didn't apply despite needing credit) fell to 5.9% from 8.2%, a series low
Voluntary account closures rose to 17.3% (highest since June 2014), involuntary lender-initiated closures to 6.7% (series high)
Expected likelihood of applying for credit over next 12 months fell to 25.5%, a series low
Consumers grew slightly more pessimistic about financial fragility: ability to raise $2,000 declined from 68.4% to 67.1%
why_it_matters: This survey captures credit market dynamics from the consumer perspective, showing that while more people are attempting to access credit (higher application rates), a larger share are being rejected. The simultaneous rise in application rates and rejection rates suggests tightening credit conditions despite increased demand. The increase in both voluntary and involuntary account closures indicates lenders are becoming more restrictive while consumers are also pulling back.
macro_context: Consumer credit access and demand serve as leading indicators for consumer spending and broader economic activity. Rising rejection rates and falling application expectations could signal future tightening in consumer credit availability. However, this is a June 2017 snapshot—nearly 9 years stale—and does not provide forward-looking market signals for current analysis purposes.
market_structure_context: Source content is a consumer credit expectations survey (Survey of Consumer Expectations - Credit Access Survey). While related to household financial conditions, it does not address market structure topics such as market plumbing, trading venue operations, clearing and settlement infrastructure, dealer intermediation, or regulatory market structure frameworks. Topic classification may need reconsideration.

25.5% — expected likelihood of applying for credit over next 12 months (series low)
67.1% — perceived ability to raise $2,000 for unexpected expense
